name: Life Sciences PhD: Genome Science and Technology
summary: Life Sciences PhD with Genome Science and Technology concentration through the Bredesen Center.
detailsNote: Bredesen application instructions explicitly select Fall 2027 and publish a December 1 final deadline in that cycle. Prior adviser contact encouraged; compulsory adviser agreement or rotation model not established. Application fee amount is not stated on the opened official pages; the program says it cannot offer fee waivers.

documents: Statement of intent, approximately 250 words or fewer per prompt
Two recommendations on letterhead as PDF/Word

english.toefl: 80 with S/W20 before January 21, 2026; 4.5 with S/W4 on/after January 22, 2026, as printed
english.note: IELTS no band below6. TOEFL Home/MyBest/Paper accepted; IELTS Online/One Skill Retake accepted. Exemption: citizenship in listed English-official country, or accredited conferred degree where English is primary instruction. Upload transcript with degree and English evidence; additional documentation if language absent. Programs may require higher scores. Central page leaves January21 boundary unclear; confirm that test date.

requirements.note: Science/engineering bachelor or master; non-STEM case-by-case, deficiencies possible. US degree GPA2.7/graduate3; non-US degree GPA3/graduate3.3. Statement covers research/career, preparation, faculty contacts and other context. Prior adviser/supervisor and most recent institution letters preferred. Contact prospective UTK/ORNL faculty about supervision/funding; report tentative commitment to admissions, which does not ensure admission. ORNL research requires site-access badge. Application fee: Bredesen Center says it cannot offer application fee waivers. Amount not established on opened sources.

funding.note: All applicants considered for Graduate Research Assistantships; no guaranteed offer, amount or international eligibility established. Prospective adviser should be asked about ability to provide financial support.
